lessons.title: The Habits That Cause Crashes

rules.text: Bad driving habits result from laziness, impatience, inattention, arrogance and aggressiveness.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Bad driving habits result from laziness, impatience, inattention,

rules.text: Always turn your head and look behind you before changing lanes, pulling out, or getting out on the traffic side.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Always turn your head and look behind you

rules.text: Come to a complete stop at a stop sign or red light regardless of traffic, even when turning right.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: a complete stop at a stop sign or red light,

lessons.plainEnglish: The handbook names five specific habits: laziness, impatience, inattention, arrogance and aggressiveness. Laziness is checking only the mirror instead of turning your head, and not bothering to signal. Impatience is rolling a stop sign because nothing is coming and someone is behind you. Inattention is letting your grip and your focus loosen until the car wanders with your mind. Arrogance is treating the car as an extension of your ego.
lessons.whyItMatters: None of these are dramatic. They are all small, comfortable shortcuts that feel harmless every time you take them, which is exactly why they turn into habits. The handbook's point is that you have to notice them in yourself and correct them deliberately.
lessons.example: You approach a red light intending to turn right. Nothing is coming and the car behind is close. Slowing to 5 mph and rolling through feels safe and considerate. It is still a failure to stop, and it is the habit that will eventually meet a pedestrian stepping off the kerb you did not check for.

lessons.title: Seeing and Being Seen

rules.text: Dim your headlight beams within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle, and within 200 feet of a vehicle you are following.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: dim your headlight beams within 500

rules.text: Turn on headlights, not just parking lights, when it begins to get dark or whenever visibility may be impaired.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: It is the law and a good idea to turn on your headlights, not just your parking

rules.text: Overdriving your headlights means driving too fast to stop within the distance they light.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: means driving too fast to stop safely within the distance clearly lit by your

lessons.plainEnglish: Two numbers matter here and they are easy to mix up: 500 feet when you are meeting someone head-on, 200 feet when you are behind them. The bigger distance goes with the bigger risk — blinding an oncoming driver puts two cars in danger. Overdriving your headlights is the subtler idea: if your lights show 200 feet of road but you need 250 feet to stop, you are driving into a space you cannot see.
lessons.whyItMatters: At night your stopping distance does not shrink, but your seeing distance does. Most drivers never adjust speed for that. And if oncoming headlights do catch you, the handbook's instruction is specific: slow down, keep right, and look at the right edge of the road rather than into the lights.
lessons.example: On an unlit road at 55 mph you meet a car. You dim at about a football field and a half away, and as it passes you fix your eyes on the white line at the right edge rather than the glare, so you keep your lane and your night vision.

lessons.title: Rain, Ice, Fog and Standing Water

rules.text: Partial hydroplaning begins at about 35 mph; at 55 mph tires can ride entirely on top of the water with no friction to brake, accelerate or corner.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: partial hydroplaning occurs on the road at about 35 mph.

rules.text: Never attempt to drive across a flooded roadway. Six inches of water can float a small vehicle; two feet will carry most away.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: As little as six (6) inches of water can float some smaller vehicles, while two

rules.text: In fog or dense smoke, reduce speed and use low-beam headlights.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Use your low-beam headlights.

lessons.plainEnglish: Rain is most dangerous when it starts, because oil and dirt lift off the surface into a slippery film before the rain washes it away. As speed rises, the tires stop cutting through water and start riding on it — around 35 mph partially, and by 55 mph potentially not touching the road at all. When that happens you have no braking, no acceleration and no steering. In fog, low beams are correct: high beams reflect off the fog straight back at you.
lessons.whyItMatters: Flooded roads deserve their own warning. Nearly half of all flash flood deaths in the United States are motorists trapped in vehicles, and in many cases the road itself has already washed away under the water. Six inches is less than the depth of a kerb.
lessons.example: A back road has water running across it after a storm. It looks shallow. You cannot see the surface underneath, you do not know whether the road is still there, and six inches is enough to float the car. You turn around.

lessons.plainEnglish: The handbook's line is blunt: you cannot safely drive 10 feet or 10 miles in an unsafe vehicle. West Virginia backs that with a two-yearly inspection and a windscreen sticker you are not allowed to remove. On the driver's side, the four conditions named are fatigue, alcohol, emotional state, and defective eyesight or hearing — and fatigue gets a specific remedy: stop every two hours for ten minutes, out of the car.
lessons.whyItMatters: Emotional state is the one people dismiss. Driving straight after a row, in tears or in a rage, is treated by the handbook as a condition affecting safe operation in the same list as alcohol and fatigue.
lessons.example: Three hours into a drive you notice you have stopped checking mirrors and cannot remember the last few miles. That is the point the handbook's two-hour rule was meant to catch. You pull in, get out, walk around for ten minutes.

lessons.plainEnglish: The handbook lists six positions another vehicle can be in before a crash: ahead of you, tailgating you, oncoming, at an angle, passing you, and being passed by you. Each has its own defence. The one people get wrong most often is being passed — treating it as a challenge instead of easing off and letting it happen causes sideswipes and run-off-road crashes.
lessons.whyItMatters: Note the handbook's test for passing: if you have to speed to pass, you probably do not need to pass. Exceeding the limit to overtake is illegal, so a pass that only works above the limit is not a legal pass.
lessons.example: Someone comes up fast behind you on a two-lane road and pulls out to pass. Rather than holding your speed, you ease off slightly and move right within your lane, which shortens the time they spend on the wrong side of the road.

questions.question: Which five bad driving habits does the handbook identify?
choices: Laziness, impatience, inattention, arrogance and aggressiveness
Speeding, tailgating, drinking, texting and fatigue
Inexperience, poor eyesight, slow reactions, nerves and distraction
Braking late, steering roughly, poor parking, stalling and drifting
questions.explanation: The handbook names these five specifically as the sources of bad driving habits, and asks you to evaluate your own behaviour against them. They are attitudes rather than manoeuvres, which is why they produce many different errors.

questions.question: A driver weaves in and out of traffic, speeds from stop to stop and tailgates. Which habit does the handbook describe?
choices: Impatience
Laziness
Inattention
Defensive driving
questions.explanation: The handbook describes the impatient driver as one who speeds from stop to stop, weaves in and out of traffic and often tailgates. It notes such a driver may be concentrating hard, yet still disrupts traffic and raises the chance of causing a crash.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, what does the handbook say you must do?
choices: Turn your head and look behind you, not rely on the mirror alone
Check the rear view mirror only
Sound your horn and move over
Rely on the blind spot monitor if fitted
questions.explanation: The handbook warns specifically against becoming lazy and looking only in the rear view mirror. You are taught to look for other traffic before changing lanes, driving away from the curb, or getting out on the traffic side — and that means turning your head.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Always turn your head and look behind you

questions.question: Which situation does the handbook say requires looking behind you for traffic?
choices: Changing lanes, driving away from the curb, or getting out on the traffic side
Only changing lanes on a highway
Only when reversing out of a parking space
Only when a passenger is in the vehicle
questions.explanation: All three are listed together in the handbook. Opening your door into traffic is included because a door opened without looking is a common cause of collisions with cyclists and passing vehicles.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: drive away from the curb, or get out of your vehicle on the traffic side.

questions.question: When does the handbook say you should signal?
choices: Before turning, changing lanes, or driving away from the curb
Only before turning at an intersection
Only when another vehicle is visible behind you
Only when changing lanes on a multi-lane road
questions.explanation: The handbook says to always signal your intention before turning, changing lanes, or driving away from the curb, and calls failing to signal a bad habit related to laziness. Combining it with not looking behind could cause a serious crash.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Always signal your intention before turning, changing

questions.question: Why does the handbook say you owe a signal to the driver behind you?
choices: Because what you do affects them, especially if you slow or stop suddenly
Because they cannot see your brake lights in daylight
Because signalling is only legally required when followed
Because it allows them to pass you safely
questions.explanation: In the tailgating vehicle situation the handbook says you have a responsibility to the driver following you to signal whenever you make a change in your driving pattern, precisely because sudden slowing or stopping affects them most.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: have a responsibility to the driver following you to signal whenever you make a change in your driving

questions.question: You are turning right on red and no cross traffic is coming. What is required?
choices: A complete stop, regardless of traffic
A rolling stop is acceptable if the way is clear
Slowing to walking pace is sufficient
No stop is needed when turning right
questions.explanation: The handbook states you must come to a complete stop at a stop sign or red light regardless of traffic, even when making a right turn. It specifically warns that pressure from following vehicles and the absence of cross traffic may tempt you to only slow down.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: a complete stop at a stop sign or red light,

questions.question: How does the handbook describe the task of driving?
choices: A full-time job with no room for daydreaming or distracting conversation
A task that becomes automatic with experience
Safe to combine with light conversation and scenery watching
Demanding only in heavy traffic
questions.explanation: The handbook says the driver's seat is no place for daydreaming, mental napping, window shopping, scenic viewing or distracting conversation, and concludes that driving an automobile is a full-time job. Lack of concentration means failing to be observant enough to avoid a crash.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: for daydreaming,  mental napping, window shopping, scenic viewing, or distracting conversation.

questions.question: Within what distance must you dim your headlights for an oncoming vehicle?
choices: 500 feet
200 feet
100 feet
1,000 feet
questions.explanation: The handbook requires dimming within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle. The larger distance applies here because high beams aimed at a driver coming towards you cause momentary blindness while both vehicles are closing at speed.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: dim your headlight beams within 500

questions.question: Within what distance must you dim your headlights when following another vehicle?
choices: 200 feet
500 feet
50 feet
300 feet
questions.explanation: When following, the handbook requires dimming within 200 feet. Your high beams reflect from the vehicle's mirrors straight into the other driver's eyes, so the rule applies even though you are behind them.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: dim your headlights within 200 feet of the

questions.question: Which pairing of headlight dimming distances is correct?
choices: 500 feet when meeting, 200 feet when following
200 feet when meeting, 500 feet when following
500 feet in both cases
200 feet in both cases
questions.explanation: Meeting takes the larger figure of 500 feet, following the smaller 200 feet. A useful way to keep them straight: the head-on case is the more dangerous one, so it gets the bigger margin.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: When following  another vehicle, dim your headlights within 200 feet of the

questions.question: What does 'overdriving your headlights' mean?
choices: Driving too fast to stop safely within the distance your headlights light up
Using high beams when low beams would do
Leaving headlights on during daylight
Fitting headlights brighter than the law allows
questions.explanation: The handbook defines it exactly this way. If your lights show 200 feet of road but you need more than that to stop, you are effectively driving blind into the space beyond them — the fix is to slow down at night, not to fit brighter bulbs.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: means driving too fast to stop safely within the distance clearly lit by your

questions.question: On an unlit road at night your low beams light about 150 feet ahead, but stopping from your current speed takes about 200 feet. What should you do?
choices: Slow down, because you are overdriving your headlights
Maintain speed, since headlights do not affect braking
Switch to parking lights to reduce glare
Speed up to shorten your time in the dark
questions.explanation: This is overdriving your headlights: you cannot stop within the distance you can see. The handbook's remedy is speed, because your stopping distance is fixed by physics while your seeing distance at night is fixed by your lights.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: A common term associated with light conditions that cause crashes is

questions.question: An oncoming vehicle's headlights are dazzling you at night. Where should you look?
choices: Well in front of your vehicle at the right edge of the road
Directly at the oncoming headlights to judge distance
At your own dashboard until the vehicle passes
At the centre line to hold your position
questions.explanation: Looking directly into oncoming headlights causes momentary blindness. The handbook says to slow down, keep to the right of your traffic lane, and look well in front of your vehicle at the right edge of the road — which keeps you positioned while preserving your night vision.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: at night, slow down, keep to the right of your traffic lane, and look well in front of your vehicle at the

questions.question: When it begins to get dark, which lights does the handbook say to use?
choices: Headlights, not just parking lights
Parking lights until full darkness
Hazard lights until full darkness
Fog lights only
questions.explanation: The handbook says it is both the law and a good idea to turn on your headlights, not just your parking lights, when it begins to get dark or any time visibility may be impaired by fog, smoke or extreme cloudiness. Turning them on a little early helps others see you.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: It is the law and a good idea to turn on your headlights, not just your parking

questions.question: When is rain generally most dangerous for traction?
choices: At the start of a light rain, when oil, dirt and water form a slippery film
After several hours of heavy rain
Once the rain has stopped and the road is drying
Only when the temperature is near freezing
questions.explanation: The handbook singles out the start of a light rain, when a mixture of oil, dirt and water forms a slippery film on the road. Heavier rain later washes that film away. The condition makes it harder to keep contact on curves and increases stopping distance.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: a mixture of oil, dirt, and water form a slippery film on the road.

questions.question: At approximately what speed does partial hydroplaning begin in a standard passenger vehicle?
choices: About 35 mph
About 15 mph
About 55 mph
About 70 mph
questions.explanation: The handbook states that up to about 35 mph most tires wipe the road like a windshield wiper, and that partial hydroplaning occurs at about 35 mph. By 55 mph the tires can ride entirely on top of the water.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: partial hydroplaning occurs on the road at about 35 mph.

questions.question: In a severe rainstorm at 55 mph, what does the handbook say happens?
choices: Tires lose all contact with the road, leaving no friction to brake, accelerate or corner
Tires grip normally as long as tread is good
Braking distance doubles but steering is unaffected
Hydroplaning cannot occur above 50 mph
questions.explanation: At 55 mph in a severe rainstorm the handbook says tires lose all contact with the road and there is no friction available to brake, accelerate or corner. A gust of wind, a curve or a slight turn can then create an uncontrollable skid.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: In a severe rainstorm, tires lose all contact with the road at 55 mph.

questions.question: Which measure does the handbook recommend to reduce the possibility of hydroplaning?
choices: Slow down and keep tires properly inflated, replacing them when tread wear indicators show
Increase speed to cut through the water
Brake firmly at the first sign of water
Let air out of the tires for a wider contact patch
questions.explanation: The handbook lists slowing down in rainstorms, on slushy roads or in standing water, and keeping tires properly inflated with adequate tread. Deep treads let water escape from under the tire and can prevent complete hydroplaning at normal highway speeds.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Keep tires properly inflated.

questions.question: You come to a roadway covered by flowing water. What does the handbook instruct?
choices: Never attempt to drive across a flooded roadway
Cross slowly in a low gear if the water looks under a foot deep
Cross quickly to avoid stalling
Follow another vehicle across to test the depth
questions.explanation: The instruction is absolute: never attempt to drive across a flooded roadway. The handbook notes that in many cases victims drive directly off the edge of an eroded road without knowing the road is no longer there.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Never attempt to drive across a flooded roadway.

questions.question: How much water can float some smaller vehicles?
choices: As little as six inches
About three feet
About two feet
At least four feet
questions.explanation: The handbook says as little as six inches of water can float some smaller vehicles, while two feet will carry most away. Once a vehicle floats into deeper water it may roll while filling, trapping everyone inside.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: As little as six (6) inches of water can float some smaller vehicles, while two

questions.question: Which statement about flooded roadways is NOT correct?
choices: Two feet of water is safe to cross in a full-size vehicle
Six inches of water can float some smaller vehicles
Flooded roads are especially dangerous at night
The road surface may have washed away beneath the water
questions.explanation: Two feet of water will carry most vehicles away, according to the handbook — it is the opposite of safe. The other three statements are all made in the handbook, including that flooded roadways are especially dangerous at night when depth is much harder to judge.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: (2) feet of water will carry most away.

questions.question: How should you brake on ice or packed snow?
choices: Gently and smoothly, releasing at the first hint the wheels are slipping
Firmly and quickly to shorten the stop
By pulling the parking brake
By downshifting only, never using the brake pedal
questions.explanation: The handbook says to always apply the brakes gently and smoothly on ice or packed snow, and to release them at the first hint the wheels are slipping. Locked wheels on ice mean no steering and no meaningful braking.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: always apply the brakes gently and smoothly.

questions.question: What is the difference between braking with and without anti-lock brakes?
choices: With ABS you keep the ability to steer while braking; without it you must pump the brakes to steer
Without ABS you keep steering; with ABS you cannot steer
ABS shortens stopping distance on ice but removes steering
There is no practical difference on ice
questions.explanation: The handbook states that in a vehicle equipped with anti-lock brakes you maintain the ability to steer while braking, but in a vehicle without them you cannot steer unless you pump the brakes, applying and releasing several times until the vehicle is under control.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: In a vehicle equipped with anti-lock brakes, you maintain the ability to steer while braking.

questions.question: Which headlights should you use in fog or dense smoke?
choices: Low beams
High beams
Parking lights only
Hazard lights instead of headlights
questions.explanation: The handbook says to use your low-beam headlights in fog or dense smoke, along with reducing speed, staying alert for an emergency stop, and using wipers to clear moisture. High beams reflect off fog back towards you and make seeing worse.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Use your low-beam headlights.

questions.question: Fog becomes too thick to see safely and you pull off the road. What else does the handbook say to do?
choices: Leave your lights on and turn on your hazard lights
Turn all lights off to avoid attracting other drivers
Leave only the interior light on
Keep driving slowly rather than stopping
questions.explanation: The handbook says that if fog or smoke impairs your vision you should pull off to the side of the road and stop, leave your lights on, and also turn your hazard lights on — so that a vehicle still moving in the fog can see where you are.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: leave your lights on and also

questions.question: How often does West Virginia require a vehicle safety inspection?
choices: Every two years
Every year
Every six months
Only when the vehicle is sold
questions.explanation: The handbook states West Virginia requires an inspection of all vehicles every two years to ensure they are in safe driving condition. When the vehicle passes, a sticker showing the month and year of the next inspection goes on the windshield.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: West Virginia requires an

questions.question: What does the inspection sticker on your windshield show, and may you remove it?
choices: The month and year of your next inspection, and removing it is against the law
The date of the last inspection, and it may be removed once expired
The inspection station's number, and it may be moved to another vehicle
Nothing of legal significance; it is advisory only
questions.explanation: The sticker shows the month and year for your next inspection, and the handbook states plainly that it is against the law for you to remove it. Inspections must be done at a station displaying an official state inspection station sign.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: It is against the law for you to remove this sticker.

questions.question: Which of these does the handbook list as a common vehicle defect that causes crashes?
choices: Unusable seat belts
Worn upholstery
A dirty engine bay
A missing spare key
questions.explanation: The handbook's list is faulty tires, brakes, lights, windshield wipers, defrosters, mufflers and exhaust system, horn, mirrors, and unusable seat belts. All are things that affect control, visibility, warning others, or protection in a crash.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Common vehicle defects that cause crashes are faulty tires, brakes, lights, windshield wipers, defrosters

questions.question: On a long trip, what rest schedule does the handbook recommend?
choices: A 10-minute break at least every two hours, spent outside the vehicle
A 30-minute break every four hours
A 5-minute break every hour, taken in the vehicle
No break is needed if you feel alert
questions.explanation: The handbook recommends a 10-minute rest break at least every two hours on a long trip, and specifies it should be spent outside the vehicle — walking around, getting a drink — rather than just sitting still.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: take a 10-minute rest break at least every two (2) hours.

questions.question: What does the handbook say fatigue does to a driver?
choices: Dulls your mind and slows your reaction time
Affects vision but not reaction time
Makes you cautious, which compensates for the tiredness
Has no measurable effect below eight hours of driving
questions.explanation: The handbook says being tired dulls your mind and slows your reaction time. If you are alone and become tired you should pull off the road and rest; if another licensed driver is available you should change drivers as soon as one becomes tired.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Being tired dulls your mind and slows your reaction time.

questions.question: You have just had a furious argument and need to drive. What does the handbook advise?
choices: Gain self control over the emotion before driving
Drive, since concentration improves when emotions are high
Drive but keep to quieter roads
Emotional state is not treated as a driving condition
questions.explanation: The handbook lists emotional state alongside fatigue, alcohol and defective eyesight or hearing as driver conditions affecting safe operation, and says you should attempt to control emotions such as anger, worry or fear and gain self control before driving.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: control these emotions and gain self control before driving.

questions.question: What should you always assume about the vehicle ahead of you?
choices: That it may stop suddenly and without warning
That it will signal before any manoeuvre
That it will maintain a steady speed
That its brake lights are working
questions.explanation: The handbook says you must always be aware that the vehicle ahead may stop suddenly and without warning, and that if you have not allowed enough following distance the result may be a crash. The defence is to stay alert and keep a safe following distance.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: the vehicle ahead of you may stop suddenly and without

questions.question: Another driver begins to pass you on a two-lane road. What does the handbook recommend?
choices: Slow down and keep as close to the right side of the road as possible
Maintain your speed so the pass is predictable
Speed up to shorten the manoeuvre
Move towards the centre line to make your position clear
questions.explanation: The handbook says not to view being passed as a challenge, and to check your mirror frequently, know what is going on around you, slow down, and keep as close to the right side of the road as possible to make it easier for the other vehicle to pass. Many sideswipe and run-off-road crashes result from being passed.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: slow down, and keep as close to the right side of the road as possible, making

questions.question: Is it legal to exceed the speed limit in order to complete a pass?
choices: No — exceeding the speed limit when passing is illegal
Yes, briefly, while alongside the other vehicle
Yes, if the other vehicle is travelling below the limit
Yes, on two-lane roads only
questions.explanation: The handbook is explicit that exceeding the speed limit when passing is illegal, and adds a useful test: if you have to speed to pass, you probably do not need to pass. There is no allowance for briefly exceeding the limit to overtake.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Exceeding the speed limit when passing is

questions.question: You are behind a vehicle doing just under the limit and could only pass by exceeding it. What does the handbook suggest?
choices: You probably do not need to pass
Pass anyway, as maintaining flow is the priority
Pass on the right instead
Sound your horn to encourage them to speed up
questions.explanation: The handbook's own words are that if you have to speed to pass, you probably do not need to pass. It also notes that passing increases wear and fuel consumption and exposes you to head-on, sideswipe and run-off-road crashes, so a marginal pass is rarely worth it.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you have to speed to pass, you probably do not need to pass.

questions.question: Which describes your duty toward a vehicle tailgating you?
choices: Signal whenever you change your driving pattern, since sudden slowing affects them most
Brake sharply to discourage them from following closely
Speed up to open a gap regardless of the limit
You owe no duty to a driver who chooses to follow too closely
questions.explanation: The handbook treats a tailgating vehicle as one of the six crash situations and puts a responsibility on you: signal whenever you make a change in your driving pattern. Brake-checking a tailgater creates the collision you are trying to avoid.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The tailgating vehicle behind you is another situation that may cause a crash.

questions.question: Which statement about stopping at a stop sign is NOT correct?
choices: A rolling stop is acceptable when there is no cross traffic
A complete stop is required regardless of traffic
A complete stop is required even when turning right
Pressure from following vehicles may tempt you to only slow down
questions.explanation: The handbook requires a complete stop regardless of traffic, including when turning right, and specifically warns that the absence of cross traffic and pressure from behind may tempt a driver to merely slow. That temptation is named as impatience.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: even when making a right turn.

questions.question: What does the handbook say lack of concentration can result in?
choices: Failure to be observant enough to avoid a crash
A citation for careless driving
Increased fuel consumption
Slower reaction only in heavy traffic
questions.explanation: The handbook states that lack of concentration can result in a driver's failure to be observant enough to avoid a crash. It calls concentration one of the most important elements of safe driving.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: of concentration can result in a driver's failure to be observant enough to avoid a crash.

questions.question: You are following a car at night on a dark road and close to within 150 feet. What must you do?
choices: Dim your headlights — the rule is within 200 feet when following
Keep high beams on, as the rule applies only to oncoming vehicles
Dim only once you are within 100 feet
Flash your high beams to signal your presence
questions.explanation: The following rule is 200 feet, so at 150 feet you are already required to dim. High beams from behind reflect off the leading driver's mirrors directly into their eyes, which is why the rule covers following as well as meeting.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: When following  another vehicle, dim your headlights within 200 feet of the

questions.question: What does looking directly into oncoming headlights cause?
choices: Momentary blindness
Improved depth perception
Eye strain but no vision loss
A temporary increase in night vision
questions.explanation: The handbook says looking directly into oncoming headlights causes momentary blindness. That is why the instruction is to look well ahead at the right edge of the road instead, keeping a visual reference while the other vehicle passes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Looking directly into oncoming headlights causes momentary blindness.

questions.question: Besides darkness, when does the handbook say to turn on your headlights?
choices: Any time visibility may be impaired, such as fog, smoke or extreme cloudiness
Only between sunset and sunrise as defined by law
Only when rain is heavy enough to need wipers
Only when other vehicles have theirs on
questions.explanation: The handbook says to turn on headlights when it begins to get dark or any time visibility may be impaired, giving fog, smoke and extreme cloudiness as examples. Turning them on a little early helps other drivers see you.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: cloudiness). If you turn on your headlights a little early, you will help other drivers see you.

questions.question: What two effects does the handbook attribute to wet pavement?
choices: Harder to keep contact with the road on curves, and increased stopping distance
Reduced tire wear and quieter running
Better grip once tires warm up
No effect provided speed is under 45 mph
questions.explanation: The handbook says the slippery film at the start of a light rain makes it harder to keep in contact with the road on curves and increases stopping distance, and tells you to reduce speed to adjust to these conditions.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: you to keep in contact with the road on curves and increases stopping distance.

questions.question: When does the handbook say tires should be replaced to help prevent hydroplaning?
choices: When tread wear indicators are visible
Every two years regardless of wear
When they are more than half worn
Only when a tire fails inspection
questions.explanation: The handbook says to replace tires when tread wear indicators are visible, and explains why: tires with deep treads allow water to escape from under the tire and can prevent complete hydroplaning at normal highway speeds.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Replace tires when tread wear indicators are visible.

questions.question: Why does the handbook say flooded roads are especially dangerous at night?
choices: It is much more difficult to judge the situation in the dark
Water freezes more readily after dark
Emergency services do not operate at night
Headlights cause water to appear shallower than it is
questions.explanation: The handbook notes flooded roadways are especially dangerous at night when it is much more difficult to see. Combined with the fact that the road surface may already have eroded away beneath the water, this is why the instruction is never to attempt a crossing.

questions.question: How should you start off on snow or ice?
choices: Keep engine speed low and accelerate slowly and smoothly
Use high engine speed to break traction free
Start in the highest available gear at full throttle
Accelerate hard briefly, then lift off
questions.explanation: The handbook says to keep your engine speed low when starting on snow or ice and to accelerate slowly and smoothly, letting the clutch out slowly in a manual. It then suggests testing the brakes while driving slowly to judge how slippery the road is.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: When starting on snow or ice, keep your engine speed low.

questions.question: Your vehicle has no anti-lock brakes and you need to steer while braking on ice. What must you do?
choices: Pump the brakes, applying and releasing until the vehicle is under control
Hold the brake pedal down firmly and steer
Use the parking brake to steer
Steering while braking is impossible in any vehicle
questions.explanation: Without ABS the handbook says you cannot steer unless you pump the brakes, applying and releasing them several times until you have the vehicle under complete control. Locked wheels cannot steer, which is exactly what ABS does automatically.

questions.question: Whose responsibility is it to keep a vehicle in proper driving condition between inspections?
choices: The driver's — the handbook says it is up to you
The inspection station's, until the sticker expires
The DMV's, through random roadside checks
The insurer's, as a condition of coverage
questions.explanation: The handbook says plainly that it is up to you to keep your vehicle in proper driving condition, then lists the common defects that cause crashes. The two-yearly inspection is a minimum check, not a substitute for maintaining the vehicle.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: It is up to you to keep your vehicle in proper driving condition.

questions.question: Where does the handbook say a rest break on a long trip should be spent?
choices: Outside the vehicle — walking around or getting a drink
In the driver's seat with the engine off
Asleep in the vehicle for at least an hour
Anywhere, provided it lasts ten minutes
questions.explanation: The handbook specifies the break should be spent outside of the vehicle, giving walking around or getting a cup of coffee or a soft drink as examples. Sitting still in the same seat does little to counter the monotony that caused the fatigue.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

questions.question: You are driving alone and become tired, with no other licensed driver available. What does the handbook say to do?
choices: Pull off the road and rest
Open the window and continue to your destination
Increase speed to arrive sooner
Continue but reduce following distance to stay engaged
questions.explanation: The handbook says if you are alone and become tired, pull off the road and rest. Measures like rolling the window down or turning the radio on are offered only as ways to reduce the monotony of driving, not as substitutes for stopping when tired.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you are alone and become tired, pull off the road and rest.

questions.question: Which four driver conditions does the handbook name as most commonly affecting safe operation?
choices: Fatigue, alcohol, emotional state, and defective eyesight or hearing
Age, inexperience, fatigue and weather
Alcohol, drugs, speed and distraction
Eyesight, hearing, reaction time and height
questions.explanation: The handbook lists exactly these four. Emotional state sitting in the same list as alcohol and fatigue is the point worth remembering — it is treated as a genuine impairment, not a mood.

questions.question: What is the defence against the vehicle ahead stopping suddenly?
choices: Stay alert, anticipate the sudden stop, and maintain a safe following distance
Drive in a different lane wherever possible
Keep your hand over the horn
Watch the vehicle's brake lights exclusively
questions.explanation: The handbook gives all three parts together: stay alert, anticipate that the driver ahead may make a sudden stop, and maintain a safe following distance. Following distance is what converts a sudden stop ahead into a non-event.

questions.question: What kinds of crash does the handbook say often result from being passed?
choices: Sideswipe and run-off-the-road crashes
Rear-end crashes only
Head-on crashes only
Rollover crashes
questions.explanation: The handbook says many sideswipe and run-off-the-road crashes result from being passed, which is why it tells you to check your mirror frequently, slow down and keep well right rather than treating the pass as a challenge.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

questions.question: Failing to signal is described by the handbook as a bad habit related to which fault?
choices: Laziness
Arrogance
Impatience
Inattention
questions.explanation: The handbook raises failing to signal under Laziness, as 'another related bad habit' alongside relying on the mirror instead of turning your head. It warns that letting the combination of these habits develop could cause a serious crash.
